script: Dinosaur fossils have been found on every continent, including Antarctica. Cryolophosaurus, a crested meat-eater, was found there in 1991. Its crest ran sideways across its head, like a comb. Back then, Antarctica was not covered in ice, and it had forests. When dinosaurs first evolved, most land was joined in one supercontinent, Pangaea. The continents have drifted far apart since then.
